item.title: Wasserstein geometry of analytic cycle spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.17496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use optimal transport to define an intrinsic distance on connected components of the Barlet space of analytic cycles on a compact K\"ahler manifold, by associating to each cycle its normalized volume measure. We prove that any two cycles in the same connected component can be joined by a deformation of finite Wasserstein length, and that the resulting metric is complete and geodesic. On the locus of smooth reduced cycles at regular parameter points, Wasserstein lengths and energies coincide with those of the normalized Weil--Petersson metric. The construction thus gives a transport interpretation of Weil--Petersson geometry and extends beyond it to components containing no smooth reduced cycles.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Cavalletti, Lorenzo Cecchi, Antonio Lerario

item.title: Extrinsic Representation of the Partial Ricci Flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.17533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The partial Ricci flow (PRF) modifies the Riemannian metric on a foliation on a distribution orthogonal to the leaves. In this work we develop extrinsic representations of PRF on geodesic foliations (twisted/warped products, weak K-contact and weak \b{eta}-Kenmotsu manifolds) and analyze model cases where PRF admits closed-form solutions. Using the convergence of PRF on model cases, we construct its extrinsic representations initialized by rotational hypersurfaces in Euclidean space as well as parallel curved surfaces and ellipsoids. The extrinsic viewpoint for PRF provides new tools for studying curvature-driven dynamics on foliations, with potential applications to calculus of moving surfaces and mathematical physics.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Rovenski, Sergey Liflandsky

item.title: Riemannian geodesic motions and null foliations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the non-collision problem: given a unit vector field $V$ on a complete Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$, under what conditions on $V$ are the maps $F_t(p)=\exp_p(tV(p))$ injective for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$? If such a vector field exists, we call it a geodesic motion on $M$. This occurs, for instance, when $V$ defines a geodesic foliation of $M$, in which case, the geodesic motion is called stationary. We show that geodesic motions on the Euclidean plane are necessarily stationary, that generic geodesic motions on round spheres are non-stationary, and that compact hyperbolic $3$-manifolds admit no geodesic motions. The non-collision problem has a Lorentzian interpretation: geodesic motions on $M$ correspond to one-dimensional null geodesic foliations of the spacetime $(M\times\mathbb{R},g-dt^2)$. In the second part of the paper, we focus on codimension-one lightlike geodesic foliations of anti-de Sitter space $\operatorname{AdS}^{1,n}$. We give a complete characterization of such foliations by means of causal curves in the Einstein universe and prove rigidity in the projective anti-de Sitter case. The last part of the paper is dedicated to the study of one-dimensional geodesic foliations of $\operatorname{AdS}^{1,2}$. We give a complete characterization when the foliation contains at least one timelike leaf.
item.dc:creator: Souheib Allout, Alaa Mohamed Boukholkhal, Lamine Messaci, Abdelghani Zeghib

item.title: Geometric Partial Differential Equations of Hydrodynamic Type for Maps into F$_\text{man}$-Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.17653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric framework for partial differential equations of hydrodynamic type on maps from a two-dimensional manifold into an F$_\text{man}$-Lie group. Using the left-invariant structure and the Maurer-Cartan form, we reduce these equations to non-linear evolution systems on the underlying F$_\text{man}$-algebra, governed by its Lie bracket and commutative associative product. We investigate the role of Poisson subalgebras, establishing that flatness of the canonical connection forces two-step nilpotency and yields a linearized evolution equation upon quotienting by the center. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a Poisson splitting and derive the corresponding tangential and transversal evolution equations. Under suitable reductivity assumptions, we show that their non-linear coupling is governed by the curvature of the canonical principal connection on the homogeneous space $G/H$. These results reveal the interplay between the algebraic structure of F$_\text{man}$-Lie groups and the geometric dynamics of hydrodynamic-type equations.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Casta\~neda-Montoya, Alexander Torres-Gomez

item.title: Numerical verification for harmonic maps: Counterexamples to Eells' conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.17697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a framework to construct harmonic maps $S^3 \rightarrow S^2$ numerically, which is used to construct approximate harmonic maps in homotopy classes with Hopf invariant $2,3,4,5,6$. By using a rigorous fixed-point argument, it is shown that there exist genuine harmonic maps with the same Hopf invariant close to these approximate solutions, thus producing a family of counterexamples to Eells' conjecture, and the related Ding's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Edward Hirst, Daniel Platt, Henrique N. S\'a Earp, Jakob Stein

item.title: One-bubble stability, reduced coefficients, and threshold compactness for the Escobar functional
item.description: arXiv:2611.17750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth compact manifold with nonempty boundary and coercive conformal energy. For $n\ge5$, in a conformal representative with $H_g=0$, we prove quantitative stability near a concentrating boundary bubble whose center stays away from the umbilic locus. The norm of the constrained gradient controls the distance to the standard bubble family with sharp exponent $1/2$, and the distance to the Lyapunov--Schmidt corrected family linearly. In the same one-bubble neighborhood, at energies at least the sharp hemisphere value $S_\ast$, the distance to the standard family is also controlled linearly. These estimates follow from the exact reduced quadratic coefficient and the scale-derivative expansion of the reduced functional. The same scale equation shows that sequences of critical points at $S_\ast$ can concentrate only at umbilic points. For $n\ge3$, a profile decomposition without a sign assumption gives Palais--Smale compactness between $S_\ast$ and the first mixed level $(S_\ast^{n-1}+Y^{n-1})^{1/(n-1)}$, where $Y=C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)$, and this endpoint is sharp. Between $S_\ast$ and the two-bubble level, we characterize noncompact levels by the lower critical values. For $n\ge7$, we obtain the fourth-order reduced expansion at umbilic centers. Under local total umbilicity, we evaluate the correction exactly, determine the conformal weight of the reduced coefficient, and obtain the optimal algebraic comparison with the squared ambient Weyl norm.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Utsab Sarkar

item.title: Stable projective immersions of K\"ahler metrics with some radial symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.18016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We combine Calabi's criterion with Pringsheim's theorem to study projective inducibility under positive rescaling. By restricting to suitable radial holomorphic curves, we obtain an obstruction to local K\"ahler immersions into finite- or infinite-dimensional complex projective space that applies uniformly to every positive rescaling. For invariant rational curves, we show that non-rationality of the moment map implies that no positive rescaling is projectively induced. We apply these criteria to the Taub-NUT, Candelas-de la Ossa, non-flat Stenzel, and Hwang-Singer scalar-flat metrics, as well as to Gibbons-Hawking metrics. Except for the Burns-Simanca metric in the Hwang-Singer family, no positive rescaling is projectively induced. For Gibbons-Hawking ALE spaces with at least two centres, the conclusion holds in every compatible complex structure. We also extend the results to complex space forms of arbitrary curvature with at least one finite signature index.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Arezzo, Andrea Loi, Giovanni Placini, Michela Zedda

item.title: Holonomy groupoids of singular subalgebroids in the non-integrable case
item.description: arXiv:2611.18160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The holonomy groupoid of a singular foliation was constructed by Androulidakis and Skandalis around 2006. The construction was later extended to singular subalgebroids of an integrable Lie algebroid, upon a choice of integrating Lie groupoid. In this work, we extend the construction of the holonomy groupoid even further, by allowing for non-integrable Lie algebroids. To do so, we make a choice of integrating local Lie groupoid $G$. When the Mal'cev completion $AC(G)$ is smooth, our construction recovers the holonomy groupoid associated with the Lie groupoid $AC(G)$. Furthermore, our holonomy groupoid has an associated $*$-algebra. We present examples in which the holonomy groupoid is realized as a quotient of the transformation groupoid of a Lie group action.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Tribouillard, Marco Zambon

item.title: Einstein contact metrics with integrable CR structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.18263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every compact Einstein contact metric manifold of dimension at least $5$ with integrable associated CR structure is Sasakian. We show that without the assumption of compactness this result does not hold: namely, for every odd dimension at least $5$, we construct an explicit noncompact Einstein contact metric manifold, with integrable CR-structure, which is not Sasakian.
item.dc:creator: Beniamino Cappelletti-Montano

item.title: Kobayashi-Hitchin Correspondence on Equivariant and Basic Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.18283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(X,J,\omega)$ be a compact complex manifold with Gauduchon metric and $G$ a Lie group acting on $X$ by holomorphic isometries. We give an explicit proof of the existence of a $G$-invariant Hermitian-Einstein metric on a $G$-polystable $G$-equivariant holomorphic vector bundle adapting the proof of L\"ubke-Teleman. We see that if $G$ is a connected complex Lie group with the bijective exponential map and the action of $G$ on $X$ is locally free, then our existence theorem is equivalent to the existence of a basic Hermitian-Einstein metric on a basic polystable basic holomorphic vector bundle on $X$ foliated by the foliation generated by the $G$-action. As an application, we can say that the foliated Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence on a Sasakian manifold $S$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-equivariant Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence on the Vaisman manifold $S\times S^1$.
item.dc:creator: Lucas H. S. Gomes, Hisashi Kasuya, Takashi Ono

item.title: The Klein-Gordon equation in projective geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.18551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss a geometric method by which H\"ormander's result on the asymptotics of a Klein-Gordon field, on an asymptotically flat spacetime, can be related to some partial peeling, \`a la Penrose, along an extended projective boundary, embedded in a spacetime with one dimension higher.
item.dc:creator: Jack Borthwick, Yannick Herfray

item.title: Algebra-Valued Yang-Mills-Type Theories: Polynomial Obstructions and Holonomy Reductions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17370v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study algebra-valued Yang-Mills-type ($A$-YMT) theories on a smooth $n$-manifold $M$, where connections take values in an $\mathfrak{m}$-graded algebra $(A, *)$ and descend to an associated bundle $E_A = P \times_\rho A \to M$. We derive the field equations, gauge transformations, and generalized Bianchi identities, showing that affine Ehresmann compatibility forces the vertical image of $\mathfrak{g}$ into the Lie nucleus $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{Lie}}(A)$ of $[x,y]_* = x*y - y*x$, and that gauge covariance and the Bianchi identity are obstructed precisely by the Jacobiator $\mathrm{Jac}_{[\cdot,\cdot]_*}$ (leaving principal $G$-gauge symmetries anomaly-free). We then prove obstructions in three settings. First, internal-product Chern-Weil and self-dual $A$-YMT functionals vanish in weak $(2,s)$-solvable algebras, invariant under $(Q,S)$-splitting extensions. Second, in reductive Cartan-Yang-Mills theories on $A = \mathbb{R}^k \oplus \mathfrak{h}$, quartic-block parenthesization yields a strict cutoff at $n \ge 8$, while binary-tree halving yields an exact Jacobsthal-number cutoff ($n - 4 \notin \bigcup_{r \ge 3}\{2 J_r, J_{r+1}\}$, plus rank vanishing for $n \ge k + 5$). We catalog Berger holonomy reductions for $4 \le n \le 7$, proving an on-shell vanishing (torsion-free) vs. off-shell survival (torsionful) dichotomy in 4D for $U(2)$ and $SU(2)$ connections---via $e \curlywedge_\rtimes (e \curlywedge_\rtimes \Omega_\omega) = \frac{1}{2}(e \curlywedge_\rtimes e) \curlywedge_\rtimes \Omega_\omega$---and in 7D for $G_2$-connections. Third, we prove an associator-quotient collapse and Jacobiator vertex dichotomy for odd-dimensional internal $A$-Chern-Simons theories, with applications to $A$-$BF$ theories, octonionic and reductive Higgs Proca mass spectra, and reductive dualities.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Ximenes Lecca, Willian Goulart Gomes Velasco

item.title: Sasakian Hodge Numbers of Calabi-Yau Links
item.description: arXiv:2611.17419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The link of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity whose degree equals the sum of its weights is a Sasakian manifold that admits a contact Calabi-Yau structure, and its Sasakian Hodge numbers are dimensions of graded pieces of the Milnor algebra of the defining polynomial. In earlier work these numbers were computed with Gr\"obner bases for the $7$-dimensional links of $7549$ of the $7555$ weighted Calabi-Yau threefold links, and two conjectures were raised from the data. The first asserts that polynomials with the same weights have Milnor algebras whose relevant graded pieces have equal dimensions; the second asserts that the Sasakian Hodge number $h^{2,1}_S$ of the link is bounded above by the Hodge number $h^{2,1}$ of the base Calabi-Yau threefold. Both conjectures are proved here. The first holds for every polynomial with an isolated singularity, because its partial derivatives form a regular sequence; an independent derivation of the Sasakian Hodge numbers by sheaf cohomology on the leaf-space orbifold is also given. For the second, the stringy Hodge numbers of the Calabi-Yau orbifold are shown to bound the middle Sasakian Hodge numbers in every dimension $n\ge2$, and for $n\ge3$ the gap in $h^{n-1,1}$ is shown to be a sum of geometric genera of loci of orbifold points; for threefolds the bound is attained exactly when all curves of orbifold points are rational. The resulting closed formulae give the Sasakian Hodge numbers of the six $7$-dimensional links left open in the earlier work and complete datasets for all $95$ five-dimensional K3 links and all $1\,100\,055$ nine-dimensional Calabi-Yau fourfold links; for the K3 links they recover the previously known second Betti numbers.
item.dc:creator: Edward Hirst, Henrique N. S\'a Earp, Tom\'as S. R. Silva

item.title: Vector bundles on spin K\"ahler surfaces and the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17647v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute new lower bounds on the second Chern class of a vector bundle $\mathscr{E}$ on a spin K\"ahler surface $X$ that satisfies $c_1(\mathscr{E}) = 0$ and $H^2(\text{End}_0\mathscr{E}) = 0.$ When $X$ is a regular elliptic surface and $\mathscr{E}$ has rank 2, our bound is sharp. Our technique is to use Furuta's finite-dimensional approximation on the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations, together with their algebro-geometric interpretation by the second named author. We also use these techniques to prove an existence theorem for singular Fueter sections and multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten solutions that holds for every Riemannian metric on a large class of 4-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Minh Lam Nguyen, Ollie Thakar

item.title: Positivity, cross-ratios, photons, and the Collar Lemma
item.description: arXiv:2409.06294v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that $\Theta$-positive representations of fundamental groups of surfaces (possibly cusped or of infinite type) satisfy a collar lemma, and their associated cross-ratios are positive. As a consequence we deduce that $\Theta$-positive representations form closed subsets of the representation variety. Along the way we systematically study a class of curves inside general flag manifolds that we call photons. Using their interplay with transversality in the flag manifold, we construct photon projections, which we use to relate the cross-ratios on the photons to the cross-ratios on the flag manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Beyrer (IRMA, UNISTRA), Olivier Guichard (IRMA, UNISTRA), Fran\c{c}ois Labourie (UniCA), Beatrice Pozzetti, Anna Wienhard

item.title: Reduction of Zieve's Conjecture on the Hurwitz problem to Three Branch Points
item.description: arXiv:2609.23663v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: M. E. Zieve conjectured that a candidate datum over the sphere is realizable whenever the gcd of the parts of every branch partition is one and it satisfies the lcm condition. We prove that this conjecture reduces to its three-branch-point case. More precisely, if every Zieve-admissible triple is realizable, then every Zieve-admissible datum with at least four branch points is realizable. As already noted by Petronio, Zieve's conjecture would imply the prime-degree conjecture of Edmonds, Kulkarni, and Stong. Song, Wen, and Zhang proved the latter conjecture in a preprint posted on arXiv in September.
item.dc:creator: Xitaiyu Liu, Tianyang Sun, Bin Xu, Yu Ye, Yi Zhou

item.title: Ahlfors--Weill Extension, Asymptotically Conformal Curves and Epstein--Poincar\'{e} Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.02171v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Ahlfors--Weill construction explicitly extends a univalent function $f$ with Schwarzian norm less than $1/2$ to a quasiconformal homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere, an extension that can be understood geometrically through Epstein surfaces. For asymptotically conformal curves, the uniformization map can be extended to a larger disk, and Loewner theory can be used to verify that this extension is quasiconformal. In this paper, we construct a local quasireflection with such an extension. Using this local quasireflection, we modify classical estimates of Ahlfors and show that domains bounded by asymptotically conformal curves have asymptotically similar hyperbolic and quasihyperbolic metrics. Furthermore, by combining these estimates with a geometric reinterpretation of the extension through Epstein surfaces, we show that the Epstein-Poincar\'e surfaces of the complementary domains are arbitrarily close to one another near the curve.
item.dc:creator: Ming Hong Tee

item.title: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
item.description: arXiv:2610.35742v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact K\"ahler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.
item.dc:creator: Tianshu Jiang, Yijian Zhang

item.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
item.description: arXiv:2611.06388v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.
item.dc:creator: Fei Yu, Junming Zhang

item.title: Holomorphic vector fields and rationality
item.description: arXiv:1911.04717v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove Carrell's conjecture that a smooth complex projective variety with a holomorphic vector field having a nonempty finite zero set is rational. The proof uses slices for projective additive group actions and a birational invariant in the dimension-graded Grothendieck ring. For a vector field with one zero, we bound the second Betti number by the dimension of the kernel of the linear part at that zero. A multiplicative group that normalizes the additive action with a nontrivial character gives a product formula for the Betti numbers and a sharp upper bound for the Euler characteristic. We classify smooth projective surfaces admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero. Among smooth projective threefolds of Picard number one admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero, there are five isomorphism types.
item.dc:creator: Wenchuan Hu, Peihan Wu

item.title: Information geometric regularization of unidimensional pressureless Euler equations yields global strong solutions
item.description: arXiv:2411.15121v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Partial differential equations describing compressible fluids are prone to the formation of shock singularities, arising from faster upstream fluid particles catching up to slower, downstream ones. In geometric terms, this causes the deformation map to leave the manifold of diffeomorphisms. Information geometric regularization addresses this issue by changing the manifold geometry to make it geodesically complete. Empirical evidence suggests that this results in smooth solutions without adding artificial viscosity. This work makes a first step towards understanding this phenomenon rigorously, in the setting of the unidimensional pressureless Euler equations. It shows that their information geometric regularization has smooth global solutions. By establishing $\Gamma$-convergence of its variational description, it proves convergence of these solutions to entropy solutions of the nominal problem, in the limit of vanishing regularization parameter. A consequence of these results is that manifolds of unidimensional diffeomorphisms with information geometric regularization are geodesically complete.
item.dc:creator: Ruijia Cao, Florian Sch\"afer

item.title: Michael-Simon inequality for anisotropic energies close to the area via multilinear Kakeya-type bounds
item.description: arXiv:2601.10647v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given an anisotropic integrand $F:\text{Gr}_k(\mathbb{R}^n)\to(0,\infty)$, we can generalize the classical isotropic area by looking at the functional $$\mathcal{F}(\Sigma^k):=\int_\Sigma F(T_x\Sigma)\,d\mathcal{H}^k.$$ While a monotonicity formula is not available for critical points, when $k=2$ and $n=3$ we show that the Michael-Simon inequality holds if $F$ is close to $1$ (in $C^1$), meaning that $\mathcal{F}$ is close to the usual area. Our argument is partly based on some key ideas of Almgren, who proved this result in an unpublished manuscript, but we largely simplify his original proof by showing a new functional inequality for vector fields on the plane, which can be seen as a quantitative version of Alberti's rank-one theorem, and we also remove a convexity assumption on $F$. As another byproduct, we also show Michael-Simon for another class of integrands which includes the $\ell^p$ norms for $p\in(1,\infty)$. For a general $F$ satisfying the atomic condition, we also show that the validity of Michael-Simon is equivalent to compactness of rectifiable varifolds.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Ars Inveniendi Analytica (2026), Paper No. 3, 33 pp
item.dc:creator: Guido De Philippis, Alessandro Pigati

item.title: Boundary Behavior of Bisectional Curvatures for Weighted Bergman Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2605.17702v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates the asymptotic boundary behavior of the holomorphic bisectional curvature for weighted Bergman metrics. By characterizing extremal functions via $L^2$-orthogonal projections, we establish an explicit formula for the weighted bisectional curvature. Utilizing the squeezing function, we then obtain quantitative upper and lower bounds for the curvature on bounded pseudoconvex domains. Furthermore, we prove that at strongly pseudoconvex boundary points, the bisectional curvature asymptotically coincides with that of the unit ball. As an application, these results provide a streamlined and unified proof for the known asymptotic behavior of the bisectional curvature of the K\"ahler-Einstein metric.
item.dc:creator: Sungmin Yoo

item.title: Regularity of critical immersions for scale-invariant curvature energies in even dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.39606v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For immersions of a closed $2h$-dimensional manifold $\Sigma$ into $\mathbb R^m$, we consider curvature energies that are invariant under ambient isometries and dilations, with the principal term $\int_{\Sigma} \big|\nabla^{(h-1)} \vec{\mathrm{I\!I}}\big|_g^2\,d\text{vol}_g$ and lower-order submanifold invariants. Following the four-dimensional approach developed in joint work with Bernard, Martino, and Rivi\`ere, we prove that every weak critical immersion in the natural Sobolev class $W^{h+1,2}$, whose induced metric and its inverse have $L^\infty$ coefficients, is real-analytic in harmonic coordinates. The proof combines geometric conservation laws, structural identities, and elliptic estimates with critical Sobolev coefficients to obtain Morrey decay and bootstrap to full regularity.
item.dc:creator: Tian Lan
